attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: It keeps the 'direct result' causal link, the shared training data and the shortage happening now. 'Peddling' is rhetoric, but the claim underneath can be checked.

contract.note: Reading 'near-identical' as little real capability difference, and 'running out' as a binding shortage, is fair. The speaker named no developers, cost measure or similarity measure, so the result depends on how those are chosen.

evidence.note: Long-term rise in training costs since 2016. Broader than 2024 and says nothing about data as the cause.
Projects public text running out between 2026 and 2032. A projection, not proof of a shortage binding in 2024.
Anonymous sources link Orion's weak coding partly to too little coding data. Supports only a narrow piece, at one developer.
Anthropic's own release claims coding gains at the same price. It cuts against 'near-identical' but is the company's word about itself and does not measure development costs.

reviews.rationale: Nothing here measures data overlap across companies or separates data limits from other causes. e3 backs a narrow data-shortage link at one developer. e4 is a company claim of capability gains. The packet cannot settle whether shared, scarce data caused rising costs and stalled capability across big tech.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. The 'allegedly' applies to the user count, not to the per-prompt losses or the adoption claim.

semantics.note: It captures both assertions: per-prompt losses and little sign of wide adoption. The speaker's contrast between ChatGPT and 'actual' generative AI software is kept by the contract, not the proposition.

contract.note: Using Q3 2024 as the period and reading 'every prompt' as unit economics is reasonable. Who counts as adopting 'actual generative AI software', and what counts as widespread, are undefined, so the result depends on the reading.

evidence.note: Company-wide annual loss forecast. It is not ChatGPT's cost per prompt, and it covers a different period.
Representative survey showing high individual use of generative AI. It includes ChatGPT, which the speaker set apart, and does not measure adoption of software products.

reviews.rationale: No ChatGPT unit economics establish per-prompt losses; company-wide losses don't measure that. The Fed survey shows wide individual use but counts ChatGPT, which the speaker excluded, and doesn't separate out software products. The packet settles neither part.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: The profitability clause is an observation. 'Few innovations coming' leans toward the future, and the drafter's 'will save' sharpens it a little. 'Atrophy' is a rhetorical premise. Treating the clause as a judgement on the visible pipeline is fair.

contract.note: Reading 'deeply' as large losses relative to revenue, and accepting that one exception does not disprove 'almost every', is fair. No list of companies, thresholds or accounting basis is given, so the result depends on the reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI's annual loss forecast as reported by the press. One company, forecast rather than actual results, and not the target quarter.
OpenAI's own report of o1's reasoning gains in the target quarter. One innovation does not refute 'few', and it shows no path to profit.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no comparable quarterly results for a broad set of well-known generative AI companies. One company's loss forecast and one company's account of its own technical progress cannot establish near-universal deep losses or a shortage of rescuing innovations.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Will undoubtedly' is a firm forecast, so it is scored. The antecedent is kept. The following 'could eliminate' sentence is hedged and rightly left out.

contract.note: Requiring measured heat-triggered throttling, rather than delays or leaks, is faithful to the speaker. Marking the condition met on secondary reports of early-deployment problems is generous, but it does not change the result.

evidence.note: Secondary report of inadequate cooling in early GB200 deployments. It bears on the antecedent only and shows no measured throttling.
CoreWeave describing its own cooling design. No throttling data either way.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated. The early-resolution rule needs a customer report showing unresolved cooling and the throttling it caused, and the packet has no such report. e1 bears at most on the antecedent. No evidence shows throttling occurring or failing to occur.
